description: Spot the sneaky thinking traps and pick the healthier thought.

1.definition: Seeing things as all good or all bad, with no middle.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You got a B on your spelling test.
1.scenarioYouDo: You got a B on your spelling test.

challenge.scenario: You got a B and think, 'I'm a total failure.' What's a truer thought?
options: 'A B means most of them were right.'
'I'm the worst speller ever born.'
'I should just quit trying at this.'

1.tip: Look for the middle ground between perfect and terrible.

2.scenarioDoneTo: You missed one shot in the game.
2.scenarioYouDo: You missed one shot in the game.

challenge.scenario: 'One miss means I should quit the team.' Better?
options: 'One miss doesn't erase every make I have.'
'One miss proves I don't belong on this team.'
'I'll never shoot the ball again after this.'

3.definition: Treating outcomes as binary and skipping the nuance.
3.scenarioDoneTo: You didn't get into your top-choice college.
3.scenarioYouDo: You didn't get into your top-choice college.

challenge.scenario: 'My future is over.' Balanced reframe?
options: 'One door closed. Still have real options.'
'That was my only path in life for me.'
'I'll just skip college entirely from here.'

3.tip: Rarely is one event the whole story.

1.definition: Imagining the worst, even when it's unlikely.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Your friend didn't wave back at you.
1.scenarioYouDo: Your friend didn't wave back at you.

challenge.scenario: 'They hate me.' Truer thought?
options: 'Maybe they didn't see me. I'll ask.'
'They definitely hate me forever now.'
'I should end the friendship first.'

1.tip: Ask 'what's most likely?' Usually it's boring.

2.definition: Jumping to the worst-case as if it's already true.

challenge.scenario: 'Something is seriously wrong with me.' Reframe?
options: 'Probably tired, thirsty, or stressed. Check first.'
'Google every disease that causes bad headaches now.'
'Assume the very worst just to be safe here.'

2.tip: The worst-case is almost never most likely.

3.definition: Spinning one bad signal into a doomsday chain.

challenge.scenario: 'Chat → fired → homeless.' Grounded reframe?
options: 'A chat could be a hundred things.'
'Update the resume and pack up now.'
'Assume the worst so I'm ready.'

3.tip: Break the doom chain. Deal with what happens.

1.definition: Guessing what someone's thinking. Usually bad guess.

challenge.scenario: 'She thinks I'm dumb.' Truer thought?
options: 'She might just be scanning the whole room.'
'She definitely thinks I'm the dumbest ever.'
'I should hide and avoid her from now on.'

1.tip: You can't read minds. Check the actual evidence.

2.definition: Treating your guess about someone as fact.

challenge.scenario: 'Everyone hates it.' More honest thought?
options: 'Most people didn't even see the post.'
'They all secretly hate the whole post.'
'I should delete it and disappear now.'

2.tip: If they haven't said it, you're guessing.

3.definition: Projecting your fears onto others as if they're truth.
3.scenarioDoneTo: A colleague was short in a meeting.
3.scenarioYouDo: A colleague was short in a meeting.

challenge.scenario: 'She wants me off the project.' Better move?
options: Ask her directly: 'Hey, everything okay?'
Assume she hates my work and quietly withdraw.
Complain about her to someone else on the team.

3.tip: Cure for mind reading: a real conversation.

1.definition: Predicting the future as if it's already true.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You have the school play tonight.
1.scenarioYouDo: You have the school play tonight.

challenge.scenario: 'I know I'll mess up.' Healthier thought?
options: 'I've practiced. I'll just do my best.'
'Fake sick and skip the whole thing.'
'I'll mess up big time, so why try?'

1.tip: You don't have a crystal ball. Future isn't written.

2.definition: So sure it fails you don't try. Never find out.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You want to ask someone to hang out.
2.scenarioYouDo: You want to ask someone to hang out.

challenge.scenario: 'They'll say no.' You don't ask. Reframe?
options: 'I don't know until I ask them.'
'They'd say no, so save the effort.'
'I'll wait for them to ask me first.'

2.tip: Assume the answer, never get the real one.

3.definition: Confusing a fear with a forecast about the future.
3.scenarioDoneTo: You want to apply for a great job.
3.scenarioYouDo: You want to apply for a great job.

challenge.scenario: 'They'll never hire me.' Reframe?
options: 'Not applying guarantees I don't get it.'
'They'd never pick me, don't waste time.'
'Wait until I feel fully qualified' (never).'

3.tip: Predicted rejection isn't real rejection. Try to know.

1.definition: Thinking something is your fault when it isn't.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Your mom seems grumpy this morning.
1.scenarioYouDo: Your mom seems grumpy this morning.

challenge.scenario: 'She's mad at me.' More likely?
options: 'She's tired or stressed. Not about me.'
'It's definitely all my fault this morning.'
'Hide out until she's cheered up again.'

2.definition: Taking blame for stuff you didn't cause.

challenge.scenario: 'It's because of me.' Truer thought?
options: 'Adults have their own stuff. Not mine.'
'If I was better they wouldn't be fighting.'
'I need to be the perfect kid always.'

2.tip: Other people's emotions belong to them.

3.definition: Taking responsibility for outcomes with many causes.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Your team missed a quarterly target.
3.scenarioYouDo: Your team missed a quarterly target.

challenge.scenario: 'It's entirely my fault.' Reframe?
options: 'What was mine? What was outside my control?'
'Yeah, it's completely on me for sure.'
'I should just quit my job right now.'

1.definition: Telling yourself you 'should' be different than you are.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You forgot your homework at home today.
1.scenarioYouDo: You forgot your homework at home today.

challenge.scenario: 'I should never forget things.' More useful?
options: 'Everyone forgets. Set a reminder for tomorrow.'
'I'm the absolute worst. I should be perfect.'
'I'll just give up on all of school now.'

2.definition: Strict inner rules that make being human feel like failing.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You're nervous before a party tonight.
2.scenarioYouDo: You're nervous before a party tonight.

challenge.scenario: 'I shouldn't feel nervous.' Healthier?
options: 'Nervous is normal. I can feel it and go.'
'I should feel absolutely nothing right now.'
'I'll just skip the whole party entirely.'

2.tip: 'Should' rules are made up. Feelings aren't wrong.

3.definition: Inherited 'shoulds' from family, culture, or old fears.

challenge.scenario: 'I shouldn't need help.' Reframe?
options: 'Getting help is a skill, not weakness.'
'Real adults handle it entirely alone.'
'I'll just push through this alone forever.'

3.tip: 'I choose to' beats 'I should' every time.

1.definition: Believing something is true just because you feel it.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You got an answer wrong in class today.
1.scenarioYouDo: You got an answer wrong in class today.

challenge.scenario: 'I feel stupid, so I AM stupid.' Truer?
options: 'Feeling it doesn't make it true.'
'The feeling IS the actual fact.'
'Never raise my hand again ever.'

1.tip: Feelings are weather, not the whole sky.

2.definition: Using emotions as proof about who you are.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You feel lonely at lunch today.
2.scenarioYouDo: You feel lonely at lunch today.

challenge.scenario: 'Feeling lonely means no one likes me.' Healthier?
options: 'Lonely right now doesn't mean no friends.'
'The feeling is the actual solid proof.'
'Give up on making friends entirely now.'

3.definition: Treating emotional experience as objective data.
3.scenarioDoneTo: You feel like a fraud at work.
3.scenarioYouDo: You feel like a fraud at work.

challenge.scenario: Feeling like a fraud despite good reviews. Reframe?
options: 'The feeling is real. Not always accurate.'
'My feelings clearly know the actual truth.'
'Quit now before they figure me out.'

3.tip: Separate the feeling from the fact.

1.definition: Slapping a big label on yourself instead of the moment.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You dropped your lunch tray at school.
1.scenarioYouDo: You dropped your lunch tray at school.

challenge.scenario: 'I'm such a loser.' Truer thought?
options: 'I dropped a tray. That's a moment, not me.'
'I really am a loser through and through.'
'I should be embarrassed about it forever now.'

1.tip: 'I did X' isn't the same as 'I AM X.'

2.definition: Turning one behavior into a whole identity.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You missed one test question today.
2.scenarioYouDo: You missed one test question today.

challenge.scenario: 'I missed one, so I'm stupid.' Healthier?
options: 'I missed one question. I'll review it later.'
'Yep, my stupidity is confirmed for good now.'
'I'll never get anything right ever again.'

3.definition: Collapsing all of you into one word.

challenge.scenario: 'I'm just unlovable.' Reframe?
options: 'One relationship ended. That's about fit, not worth.'
'Nobody could ever really love someone like me.'
'I'll definitely be alone completely from now on.'

3.tip: No one word is you. Zoom in instead.

1.definition: Brushing off good stuff. 'It doesn't count.'
1.scenarioDoneTo: You got an A on your project.
1.scenarioYouDo: You got an A on your project.

challenge.scenario: 'It was probably easy. Doesn't count.' Healthier?
options: 'I worked hard. Let this one count.'
'It was easy, so it doesn't really matter.'
'Literally anyone could have done that.'

1.tip: Wins count, even when it feels awkward.

2.definition: Explaining away positives so they can't build you up.

challenge.scenario: 'They're just being nice.' Reframe?
options: 'Say thanks. Let it actually land.'
'They didn't really mean any of it.'
'Argue with them about it right now.'

3.definition: A filter that only lets negatives count as evidence.
3.scenarioDoneTo: You just got a big promotion.
3.scenarioYouDo: You just got a big promotion.

challenge.scenario: 'They just needed to fill the role.' Reframe?
options: 'They picked me over others. That's earned.'
'It was purely luck, plain and simple.'
'I really don't deserve any of this.'

3.tip: Count wins with the same rigor as losses.

1.definition: Focusing on one bad thing and ignoring the good stuff.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You had a fun day but got teased once.
1.scenarioYouDo: You had a fun day but got teased once.

challenge.scenario: One tease ate the whole day. Truer picture?
options: 'Lots of good AND one bad thing. Both real.'
'That one tease ruined the whole entire day.'
'My whole day was actually terrible.'

1.tip: Widen the lens. Ask 'what else happened?'

2.definition: Picking one negative detail and letting it define everything.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You played 9 songs well and hit 1 wrong note.
2.scenarioYouDo: You played 9 songs well and hit 1 wrong note.

challenge.scenario: You obsess over the wrong note. Healthier?
options: '9 out of 10 were great. One miss is fine.'
'That wrong note ruined the whole entire recital.'
'I'll never perform in front of people again.'

2.tip: Count the whole scoreboard, not just the miss.

3.definition: Selective attention to negatives that warps your self-story.
3.scenarioDoneTo: Your review had 20 positives and 2 growth notes.
3.scenarioYouDo: Your review had 20 positives and 2 growth notes.

challenge.scenario: You spiral on the 2 negatives. Reframe?
options: 'Both parts are useful. Neither cancels the other.'
'The 2 negatives are the actual real review here.'
'The 20 positives were basically just filler notes.'

3.tip: Read the whole page. Growth notes aren't a verdict.

1.scenarioDoneTo: One kid said no to playing today.
1.scenarioYouDo: One kid said no to playing today.

challenge.scenario: 'Nobody EVER wants to play.' Truer?
options: 'One no today. Doesn't mean everyone forever.'
'Nobody will ever want to play with me again.'
'I'll play alone forever for the rest of time.'

2.definition: One event becomes a lifelong pattern in your head.
2.scenarioDoneTo: One crush wasn't interested in you.
2.scenarioYouDo: One crush wasn't interested in you.

challenge.scenario: 'This ALWAYS happens. I'll NEVER find someone.' Reframe?
options: 'One person, one moment. Just a data point.'
'Nobody will ever really want to be with me.'
'This is basically my whole life story now.'

2.tip: A sample of 1 isn't a pattern.

3.scenarioDoneTo: One pitch didn't land in the meeting.
3.scenarioYouDo: One pitch didn't land in the meeting.

challenge.scenario: 'I'm bad at pitching — always will be.' Reframe?
options: 'This pitch, this audience, this specific day.'
'I'm just bad at this forever, no matter what.'
'Never pitch anything again for the rest of my life.'

1.definition: Measuring yourself against others and losing.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Your classmate got the lead role.
1.scenarioYouDo: Your classmate got the lead role.

challenge.scenario: 'They're better at everything.' Truer thought?
options: 'Better at this. I'm good at other things.'
'They win at everything, I lose at everything ever.'
'I should just give up on doing any plays.'

1.tip: Compare you before vs. after. Not you vs. them.

2.definition: Measuring your life against everyone's highlight reel.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You're scrolling social media at night.
2.scenarioYouDo: You're scrolling social media at night.

challenge.scenario: 'Everyone seems happier than me.' Reframe?
options: 'My behind-scenes vs. their highlight reel.'
'They really are all better than me at life.'
'I should sit here and feel bad about myself.'

2.tip: Feeds are edited. Nobody posts the boring.

3.definition: Comparing your inner doubt to others' outer output.
3.scenarioDoneTo: A peer just launched a company.
3.scenarioYouDo: A peer just launched a company.

challenge.scenario: 'I'm so far behind.' Reframe?
options: 'Different lanes, different timing. Mine works.'
'I really am behind at life, no doubt about it.'
'I should just quit trying entirely from here.'

1.definition: Small problems feel huge. Strengths feel tiny.
1.scenarioDoneTo: You forgot one word in your presentation.
1.scenarioYouDo: You forgot one word in your presentation.

challenge.scenario: 'That was the WORST ever.' Truer thought?
options: 'Awkward for a second. Nobody will remember.'
'They'll remember this forever and ever now.'
'I can never do another presentation ever.'

1.tip: Will this matter in a week? A month?

2.definition: Microscope on flaws, telescope on strengths.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You got four A's and one C.
2.scenarioYouDo: You got four A's and one C.

challenge.scenario: You focus 100% on the C. Reframe?
options: '4 A's and 1 C. One area to improve.'
'The C ruined the entire report card for me.'
'I must actually be really bad at school.'

2.tip: Same magnification for wins and losses. Fair.

3.scenarioDoneTo: You had a great quarter with one complaint.
3.scenarioYouDo: You had a great quarter with one complaint.

challenge.scenario: One complaint erases a great quarter. Reframe?
options: 'Great quarter plus one issue. Both are true.'
'The complaint is basically the whole story here.'
'The entire quarter was a real failure for me.'

3.tip: Size things accurately. Big things big.

1.scenarioDoneTo: Your team lost a game today.
1.scenarioYouDo: Your team lost a game today.

challenge.scenario: 'It's YOUR fault!' What's healthier?
options: 'We lost as a team. What can we fix?'
'It's all their fault, no doubt about it.'
'Never playing with them again for sure.'

1.tip: Blame ends teams. Problem-solving builds them.

2.definition: Placing 100% of the cause outside or inside yourself.

challenge.scenario: 'The teacher is TERRIBLE. Her fault.' More accurate?
options: 'Some teaching plus I didn't prep enough.'
'She's entirely to blame here, all of it.'
'Nothing I do would help me here at all.'

2.tip: Ask: my share? Theirs? The situation?

3.definition: Attribution swings between 'all me' and 'all them.'

challenge.scenario: You swing 'all them' or 'all me.' Reframe?
options: 'My part, their part, context. All useful info.'
'Just blame someone else for the whole thing.'
'Take 100% blame myself for all of it.'

1.definition: Getting stuck on unfair when nothing can change.
1.scenarioDoneTo: Your sibling got a bigger piece of cake.
1.scenarioYouDo: Your sibling got a bigger piece of cake.

challenge.scenario: 'That's not fair!' What's helpful next?
options: 'Mention it calmly, then enjoy my own slice.'
'Just ruin dessert for absolutely everyone here.'
'Stay mad about this forever and ever now.'

1.tip: Act if you can. Move on if you can't.

2.definition: Ruminating on unfairness turns it into resentment.
2.scenarioDoneTo: You worked hardest but got the same group grade.
2.scenarioYouDo: You worked hardest but got the same group grade.

challenge.scenario: You stay furious for weeks. Reframe?
options: 'Unfair. Name it. Learn. Stop owning it.'
'I'll just be really mad about this forever.'
'Never do group work with anyone ever again.'

2.tip: Naming unfair is fine. Living in it hurts you.

3.definition: 'The world owes me fair' sets up chronic resentment.
3.scenarioDoneTo: A colleague got promoted before you.
3.scenarioYouDo: A colleague got promoted before you.

challenge.scenario: You're still bitter months later. Reframe?
options: 'It was unfair. Now what's my next move?'
'Just stay bitter and hope karma hits them.'
'Nothing will ever be fair in this life for me.'

3.tip: 'Unfair' can be true AND I still choose next.

challenge.scenario: 'I'm in HUGE trouble!' Healthier?
options: 'Could be a hundred things. I'll find out.'
'Definitely prepare for the very worst outcome.'
'Hide out until they just forget about it.'

1.tip: Wait for real info before deciding what happened.

2.definition: Guessing what people think AND how it ends.
2.scenarioDoneTo: Your crush hasn't texted back in 20 minutes.
2.scenarioYouDo: Your crush hasn't texted back in 20 minutes.

challenge.scenario: 'Ghosted forever.' Truer thought?
options: 'People are busy. 20 minutes is nothing.'
'Definitely ghosted, no question about it now.'
'Never text this person ever again after this.'

3.definition: Your brain fills blanks with the loudest guess.
3.scenarioDoneTo: An email from HR is marked 'sensitive.'
3.scenarioYouDo: An email from HR is marked 'sensitive.'

challenge.scenario: 'I'm being fired.' Reframe?
options: 'HR emails cover a lot. I'll read it first.'
'Update the resume right now, don't wait for it.'
'Confront my manager preemptively about it now.'

3.tip: Open the email. Fear guesses worse than reality.

1.scenarioDoneTo: It rained on your birthday party.
1.scenarioYouDo: It rained on your birthday party.

challenge.scenario: 'I ruined it.' Truer thought?
options: 'Weather isn't mine. Fun indoors instead.'
'I somehow ruined the whole day for everyone.'
'Nothing good ever really happens to me anyway.'

1.tip: Sort what you control from what you don't.

2.definition: Trying to manage everyone's feelings all the time.
2.scenarioDoneTo: There's some tension in your friend group.
2.scenarioYouDo: There's some tension in your friend group.

challenge.scenario: 'I have to keep everyone happy.' Healthier?
options: 'I influence the vibe. Not everyone's feelings.'
'It's all on me to fix this for everyone now.'
'Make everyone happy always, no matter what.'

2.tip: Own your part, not everyone else's.

3.definition: Over-control burns you out; under-control makes helpless.
3.scenarioDoneTo: You're micromanaging every part of a project.
3.scenarioYouDo: You're micromanaging every part of a project.

challenge.scenario: 'Only I can do it right.' Reframe?
options: 'What can I delegate plus coach vs. own?'
'Only I can actually do it correctly here.'
'Just give up and disengage from all of it.'
